newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson Cos Ltd up after Novamax sale.
newsitem.headline: Molson Cos Ltd up after Novamax sale.

text.p: Shares in Molson Cos Ltd rose on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday after the Canadian brewing and sports giant agreed to sell its Novamax Technologies unit to Henkel KGaA for C$255 million.

The sale completes Molson's bid to end a troubled foray into specialty chemicals and return to its 210-year-old brewing roots. Molson's class A stock was up 0.25 at 19.65 in late morning turnover of 38,095 shares.
"We're pleased with the result of this final stage of the divestment of the Diversey group of companies," said Brian Crombie, Molson's senior-vice president of corporate finance.
Molson said it expects a definitive deal to be signed with Henkel on or before October 9.

Earlier this year, Molson sold most of Diversey's worldwide cleaning and sanitizing businesses to British/Dutch giant Unilever Plc for C$780 million. It also sold Diversey's money-losing U.S. institutional and commercial laundry business to a management-led group.
In May, Illinois-based Nalco Chemical Co picked up Diversey Water Technologies for C$112 million.
With the Novamax sale, Crombie said the Diversey divestiture will put about C$1.2 billion in Molson's coffers.
Molson has used C$467 million to pay down debt and another C$100 million is being reserved for costs and contingencies, Crombie said.
"The balance -- we are investigating opportunities to invest it in the world of international beer. If we don't have any value-creating opportunities we'll return it to shareholders," Crombie said.

He said the search for a brewing investment has been slow because Molson has devoted most of its attention to selling off its Diversey units. With the divestiture over, Molson has said it will focus on opportunities in China and Latin America.

"We are looking strongly at Latin America and Chinese markets. Any sizeable investment we would make would be with partners or as a joint venture," Molson's new president and chief executive officer Norman Seagram told reporters at the company's annual meeting in September.

Molson has expressed interest in buying a larger stake in Molson Breweries, its 40-percent-owned brewing unit. The brewer is also 40-percent-owned by Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and 20-percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc's Miller Brewing unit. But neither Foster's nor Miller appear willing to sell their stakes, Crombie said.
